title: Runtime Polymorphism in Action
summary: Master runtime polymorphism in real-world systems: processing heterogeneous collections, decoupling caller logic from subclass variants, and writing extensible code.
learningObjectives: Design systems utilizing heterogeneous collections through parent-type arrays and lists
Eliminate fragile if-else / switch type-checking chains using dynamic dispatch
Apply the Open-Closed Principle by introducing new subclasses without changing client processing loops
Avoid common performance and downcasting pitfalls in polymorphic iteration
expectedOutcomes: You can build batch processing pipelines accepting arrays of base classes and dynamically executing subclass behaviors
You can refactor procedural conditional branches into elegant polymorphic object hierarchies

activities.title: Everyday Analogy: The Universal Media Player

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: A modern smart TV connects to gaming consoles, Blu-ray players, cable set-top boxes, and USB thumb drives through HDMI ports. The remote control has a single 'Play/Pause' button. When you tap 'Play', the TV sends a uniform play signal down the active connection. It does not contain specialized hardware for each device manufacturer; each connected device interprets the play command according to its own firmware.
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: The HDMI port is the parent reference type (common contract). The connected devices are diverse subclass instances (PlayStation, Blu-ray, AppleTV). Tapping Play is invoking an overridden method. Dynamic dispatch routes the command to the actual device firmware at runtime.
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: The client (TV remote) never cares which concrete brand is attached—it issues uniform requests, and runtime polymorphism ensures the correct specialized behavior occurs seamlessly.

activities.title: Decoupling Systems with Runtime Polymorphism
Heterogeneous Shape Pipeline with Dynamic Calculation
activities.explanation: Notice how describe() in Shape calls calculateArea(). Even though describe() is written in the superclass, calling it on a Circle resolves calculateArea() dynamically to Circle's implementation!

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: Array of base type `Shape[]` is instantiated with concrete instances of Circle and Rectangle.
The for-each loop iterates over each element using reference variable `Shape s`.
Inside `s.describe()`, the base class method invokes `this.calculateArea()`. Because `this` is dynamically bound, Circle's Math.PI formula is executed for circles, and width * height for rectangles.
The accumulator aggregates total area without needing to know any geometric specifics of individual shapes.

activities.title: Polymorphic Notification Service
activities.explanation: NotificationDispatcher.broadcast takes a Notification reference. If a developer later introduces SlackNotification, broadcast() requires zero modifications.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: Parent class `Notification` defines base signature `send(String, String)`.
The client service `NotificationDispatcher` operates strictly on the abstract `Notification` parameter.
At runtime, invocation `channel.send(...)` executes EmailNotification or SMSNotification based on the actual object passed.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural advantage of runtime polymorphism?
options: Faster JVM startup execution time
Decoupling client code from concrete implementations, enabling easy extension without modification
Automatic memory garbage collection optimization
Elimination of static variables and methods in child classes
questions.explanation: Runtime polymorphism allows client code to interact with high-level parent abstractions, enabling new child types to be plugged in without changing existing client loops or callers.

questions.question: Given `Shape[] arr = { new Circle(), new Square() };`, what happens when `arr[i].draw()` is called in a loop?
options: Shape's draw() method always executes because the array type is Shape
A ClassCastException is thrown at runtime unless explicit casting is performed
The JVM looks up the vtable of each specific element at runtime and executes Circle's or Square's draw()
Compilation error: cannot store subclasses in a superclass array
questions.explanation: Java arrays of reference types are covariant. The JVM resolves overridden instance methods using each object's actual class vtable at runtime.

questions.question: Why is replacing a polymorphic method call with an `if-else (obj instanceof SubClass)` chain considered an anti-pattern?
options: `instanceof` always throws a NullPointerException on valid objects
It tightly couples the caller to every concrete subclass and violates the Open-Closed Principle
Java forbids using instanceof in for loops
It converts dynamic binding to static compilation errors
questions.explanation: Explicit type checking means whenever a new subclass is created, every `if-else` chain must be manually updated, leading to brittle, error-prone code.

questions.question:
In the code: `class P { void show() { System.out.print("P"); } } class C extends P { void show() { System.out.print("C"); } }`
What is printed by: `P[] list = { new P(), new C() }; for(P p : list) p.show();`?
options: PP
PC
CC
Compilation error
questions.explanation: `list[0]` is a P instance, so `p.show()` invokes P's method ('P'). `list[1]` is a C instance, so dynamic dispatch invokes C's method ('C'). The output is 'PC'.

questions.question: If a superclass method `process()` is called inside another superclass method `run()`, what happens if a subclass overrides `process()`?
options: The superclass version of process() always runs because run() was defined in superclass
The subclass overridden version of process() runs when invoked on a subclass object
A StackOverflowError occurs automatically
Compilation error: superclass methods cannot call overridden methods
questions.explanation: Inside `run()`, the implicit receiver is `this`. When invoked on a child instance, dynamic method dispatch ensures `this.process()` routes to the child's overridden version.

questions.question: Which of the following is REQUIRED for runtime polymorphism to work?
options: The method must be static
The method must be private in the parent class
An inheritance relationship with method overriding and method invocation via a parent reference
The child class must have more fields than the parent class
questions.explanation: Runtime polymorphism requires inheritance, method overriding, and invocation via a reference variable pointing to a child object.

questions.question: What is array covariance in Java (e.g., `Parent[] arr = new Child[5];`) and what risk does it carry at runtime?
options: It allows zero memory overhead for primitives
It allows storing non-Child objects into arr if compiled, but throws ArrayStoreException at runtime
It prevents garbage collection of child instances
It converts all child objects to parent objects irreversibly
questions.explanation: Java arrays are covariant: `Child[]` is assignable to `Parent[]`. However, attempting to insert an incompatible sibling object throws `ArrayStoreException` at runtime.

questions.question: Can runtime polymorphism be achieved with instance fields (variables)?
options: Yes, variables are overridden dynamically just like methods
No, variables are resolved at compile-time based on the reference type (variable hiding)
Only if the variable is declared protected
Only if the variable is marked final
questions.explanation: Fields are NOT polymorphic in Java. Field access is resolved at compile time according to the reference type.

questions.question: What happens if a parent class reference in a heterogeneous array is `null` when a polymorphic method is called?
options: The parent's default method executes
A NullPointerException is thrown at runtime
The loop skips the null element silently
The child's default constructor is called
questions.explanation: Attempting to invoke an instance method on a `null` reference immediately triggers a `NullPointerException` before dispatch can occur.

questions.question: How does the Open-Closed Principle relate to runtime polymorphism?
options: Classes should be closed to inheritance and open to public fields
Software entities should be open for extension (adding new subclasses) but closed for modification (existing client logic remains unchanged)
Methods must always be private to close external access
Classes must be final so nobody can modify them
questions.explanation: The Open-Closed Principle states that software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification. Runtime polymorphism is the primary mechanism to achieve this in OOP.

interviewQA.question: How does runtime polymorphism help implement the Open-Closed Principle (OCP)?
interviewQA.answer: Runtime polymorphism allows high-level business workflows (such as order fulfillment or checkout) to depend on abstract superclasses or interfaces. When a new fulfillment channel or payment provider is introduced, developers create a new subclass overriding standard operations. The consumer workflow requires zero code changes or recompilations, remaining closed for modification while cleanly extended.

interviewQA.question: Why is the use of `instanceof` with cascading `if-else` blocks considered a code smell in object-oriented systems?
interviewQA.answer: Using cascading `if-else (x instanceof Subclass)` blocks couples the caller to concrete implementations, violates the Open-Closed Principle, and scatters type-checking logic across the codebase. Every time a new subclass is added, developers must find and modify every corresponding `if-else` statement. Polymorphism replaces this with a single method call dynamically dispatched to the target object.

interviewQA.question: What happens under the hood when a method in a heterogeneous array `SuperClass[]` is invoked?
interviewQA.answer: At runtime, when the JVM executes `invokevirtual`, it retrieves the actual runtime type from the object header of the current array element. It reads the method pointer from the class vtable (Virtual Method Table) corresponding to that method offset and jumps directly to that machine code, executing the overridden child implementation.

interviewQA.question: Can you achieve runtime polymorphism if the superclass method is declared `private` or `final`?
interviewQA.answer: No. `private` methods are not inherited and cannot be overridden (they use `invokespecial`). `final` methods explicitly forbid overriding (enforced at compile time). In both cases, runtime polymorphism is impossible because no child implementation can replace the method.

interviewQA.question: Explain array covariance in Java and the runtime exception it can cause.
interviewQA.answer: Java arrays are covariant: `Integer[]` is a subtype of `Number[]`, and `Child[]` is a subtype of `Parent[]`. If code casts `Child[]` to `Parent[]` and attempts to assign an instance of another sibling subclass `arr[0] = new Sibling()`, the compiler permits it based on `Parent[]`, but the JVM checks the actual array component type at runtime and throws `java.lang.ArrayStoreException`.

interviewQA.question: How does runtime polymorphism impact runtime performance in latency-critical applications?
interviewQA.answer: Polymorphic calls introduce a minor indirect pointer lookup via the object's vtable. Modern HotSpot JVMs optimize this heavily using monomorphic call site devirtualization (inlining the call if only one concrete class is observed at runtime) and bimorphic inlining. In megamorphic call sites (3+ active concrete types at the same call site), vtable lookup occurs without inlining, adding a few CPU cycles.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I can instantiate and manage heterogeneous collections of objects using a common superclass array.
I understand why iterating through a superclass collection dynamically invokes the appropriate child method.
I know how runtime polymorphism eliminates brittle `instanceof` conditional ladders.
I understand how the Open-Closed Principle is enabled by polymorphic dispatch.
I know that invoking `this.method()` from within a superclass method resolves dynamically to child overrides.
I understand the difference between array covariance and runtime `ArrayStoreException`.
I know that `null` references in a polymorphic collection throw `NullPointerException` when methods are invoked.
I understand how the HotSpot JVM optimizes monomorphic vs megamorphic call sites.
I can design an extensible service dispatcher accepting base class parameters.
I know that instance fields are not polymorphic and do not participate in dynamic dispatch.

practiceProblems.title: Polymorphic Transport Fleet
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Move vehicles using runtime polymorphism:

1. Class Vehicle:
   - Field: protected String model
   - Constructor: Vehicle(String model)
   - Method: public void move() printing 'Vehicle moving'

2. Subclasses extending Vehicle:
   - Class Car: constructor(model), @Override move() printing '<model> drives on road at 60 mph'
   - Class Bicycle: constructor(model), @Override move() printing '<model> pedals on bike lane at 15 mph'

Test in Main:
Vehicle v1 = new Car("Tesla"); Vehicle v2 = new Bicycle("Trek");
Call v1.move(); and v2.move();.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Tesla drives on road at 60 mph
Trek pedals on bike lane at 15 mph
hints: In Car and Bicycle, annotate move() with @Override.
Loop over Vehicle[] fleet with a standard for-each loop: for(Vehicle v : fleet) v.move();
practiceProblems.description: Move cars and bicycles through a common Vehicle parent reference.

practiceProblems.title: Payroll Tax Calculation Engine
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Calculate taxes for diverse taxpayers from scratch:

1. Class TaxPayer:
   - Fields: protected String name, protected double grossIncome
   - Constructor: TaxPayer(String name, double grossIncome)
   - Method: public double calculateTax() returning grossIncome * 0.15 (15% base tax)

2. Subclasses extending TaxPayer:
   - Class SmallBusiness: @Override calculateTax() returning (grossIncome * 0.20) - 1200.0
   - Class Freelancer: @Override calculateTax() returning (grossIncome * 0.10) - 500.0

Test in Main:
TaxPayer[] payers = {
  new TaxPayer("Alice", 60000.0),
  new SmallBusiness("Bob", 30000.0),
  new Freelancer("Charlie", 50000.0)
};
Loop through payers and print '<name>: $' + p.calculateTax().
hints: In SalariedEmployee, check if grossIncome > 50000 to compute the bracket math.
Loop over TaxPayer[] and call tp.calculateTax() dynamically.
practiceProblems.description: Calculate individual, small business, and freelance taxes using a TaxPayer array from scratch.

practiceProblems.title: Dynamic Audio Effect Processor
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Apply audio filters using runtime polymorphism from scratch:

1. Class AudioFilter:
   - Method: public String process(String sample) returning '[Raw] ' + sample

2. Subclasses extending AudioFilter:
   - Class EchoFilter: @Override process(String s) returning '[Echo: ' + s + ' ... ' + s + ']'
   - Class ReverbFilter: @Override process(String s) returning '[Reverb: ~' + s + '~]'
   - Class NoiseGateFilter: @Override process(String s) returning '[Gated: ' + s + ']'

Test in Main:
AudioFilter[] rack = { new EchoFilter(), new ReverbFilter(), new NoiseGateFilter() };
Loop through rack and print filter.process("Vocals_Take1").
hints: Each subclass overrides the process(String sample) method with its custom formatting.
In main, iterate over AudioFilter[] and print the result of filter.process(sample).
practiceProblems.description: Process audio clips through an array of different sound filters from scratch.

practiceProblems.title: Fix Broken Polymorphic Discount System
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Fix the discount calculation system:

Bug: In the provided code, `applyDiscount()` is static in DiscountPolicy. Static methods do not override dynamically!

Your Task:
1. Remove `static` from `applyDiscount(double total)` in DiscountPolicy, StudentDiscount (20% off), and VipDiscount (30% off).
2. Add `@Override` in StudentDiscount and VipDiscount.

Test in Main:
DiscountPolicy p1 = new StudentDiscount(); print p1.applyDiscount(100.0);
DiscountPolicy p2 = new VipDiscount(); print p2.applyDiscount(100.0);
hints: Remove the static keyword from applyDiscount in all classes.
Add @Override annotations in StudentDiscount and SeniorDiscount.
practiceProblems.description: Fix broken code where discounts were computed with static methods, preventing polymorphism from working.

practiceProblems.title: SQL Query Pagination Generator
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Generate SQL pagination queries for different databases from scratch:

1. Class SqlDialect:
   - Method: public String paginate(String query, int offset, int limit) returning query + ' FETCH FIRST ' + limit + ' ROWS ONLY'

2. Subclasses extending SqlDialect:
   - Class MySqlDialect: @Override paginate(q, off, lim) returning q + ' LIMIT ' + off + ', ' + lim
   - Class PostgresDialect: @Override paginate(q, off, lim) returning q + ' LIMIT ' + lim + ' OFFSET ' + off
   - Class OracleDialect: @Override paginate(q, off, lim) returning 'SELECT * FROM (' + q + ') WHERE ROWNUM <= ' + lim

Test in Main:
SqlDialect[] dialects = { new MySqlDialect(), new PostgresDialect(), new OracleDialect() };
Loop through dialects and print d.paginate("SELECT * FROM users", 10, 5).
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 10, 5
SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 5 OFFSET 10
SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM users) WHERE ROWNUM <= 5
hints: In each dialect, override paginate(String query, int offset, int limit) with dialect-specific SQL syntax.
Iterate over the array of SqlDialect references and invoke paginate on each.
practiceProblems.description: Generate database-specific pagination syntax (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle) through a SqlDialect parent reference from scratch.
